tools.name: GNPS
tools.summary: A web-based ecosystem for sharing, searching, annotating, and organizing tandem mass spectrometry data, including spectral-library search and molecular networking.
common_uses: Search experimental MS/MS spectra against community spectral libraries.
Build classical or feature-based molecular networks.
Share datasets, libraries, workflows, and analysis results with collaborators or the public.

designed_for: MS/MS-centered annotation, molecular networking, public-data search, and community sharing of metabolomics and natural-products data.
requirements: Most workflows require centroided/open mass-spectrometry formats and appropriate metadata or feature tables for the selected analysis.
considerations: GNPS is an ecosystem rather than a single algorithm; users should cite and report the specific workflow, version or task URL used.

tools.description: GNPS is an open web ecosystem for community analysis, organization, searching, annotation, and sharing of tandem mass-spectrometry data. It hosts spectral libraries and multiple analysis workflows, including molecular networking and repository-scale search, and interoperates with public MassIVE datasets and structured sample metadata.

tools.name: MassIVE
tools.summary: A public repository for depositing, preserving, browsing, downloading, and reusing mass-spectrometry datasets, including datasets connected to GNPS analyses.
tools.description: MassIVE is a community repository for the public exchange of mass-spectrometry data. It stores raw and processed files, metadata and publication-associated datasets, and supports browsing, downloading, accessioned deposition, and reuse through GNPS and related services.
common_uses: Deposit publication-associated mass-spectrometry datasets.
Browse and download public mass-spectrometry data for reuse and reanalysis.

designed_for: Long-term deposition and public reuse of mass-spectrometry datasets.
requirements: Data and metadata must be uploaded and a dataset explicitly made public when public access is intended.
considerations: Dataset-level metadata quality affects downstream discoverability and reanalysis.

tools.name: MassQL
tools.summary: An open-source domain-specific query language for expressing and running searches over mass spectrometry data using MS-focused syntax.
common_uses: Search local or repository-scale mass spectrometry datasets for precursor, fragment, neutral-loss, and intensity patterns.
Express reusable MS queries in a human-readable text format.

tools.name: MASST
tools.summary: A GNPS web search tool that queries an MS/MS spectrum across public mass-spectrometry datasets and spectral libraries to identify where related spectra occur.
tools.description: MASST performs repository-scale searching of a query tandem mass spectrum against public GNPS/MassIVE data and spectral libraries. It is designed to place a spectrum in biological or environmental context by identifying datasets and files in which related fragmentation spectra occur.
common_uses: Search a query MS/MS spectrum across public GNPS datasets.
Identify datasets, files, and public-library spectra related to a query spectrum.

designed_for: Repository-scale contextualization of individual MS/MS spectra.
requirements: A centroided query MS/MS spectrum with precursor information.
considerations: Search tolerances and similarity thresholds affect which public matches are returned.

tools.name: MetaboAnalyst
tools.summary: A web platform and associated R package for metabolomics data processing, statistical analysis, visualization, functional interpretation, and multi-omics integration.
common_uses: Perform exploratory and inferential statistics on metabolomics data tables.
Generate visualizations and pathway-level interpretations.
Integrate metabolomics with transcriptomics or other omics results.

tools.name: MS-DIAL
tools.summary: A graphical and command-line workbench for untargeted metabolomics and lipidomics data processing across multiple chromatography and mass spectrometry platforms.

access.notes: The software, source, and associated libraries are publicly accessible; users should confirm the license and terms that apply to the specific component and version they use.

common_uses: Process untargeted LC-MS, GC-MS, and lipidomics datasets through a graphical workflow.
Deconvolute data-independent MS/MS spectra and match features against spectral libraries.

designed_for: Broad untargeted metabolomics and lipidomics processing through a graphical workflow across several chromatography and MS acquisition modes.
Datasets requiring deconvolution and interpretation of data-independent or all-ion MS/MS signals.
requirements: Users should confirm current operating-system support and input-format compatibility for the version they install.
considerations: Large libraries and highly permissive annotation settings can increase candidate identifications; confidence levels and library provenance should be reported.

tools.description: MS-DIAL is a metabolomics and lipidomics workbench designed for broad-spectrum processing of chromatography–mass-spectrometry datasets. It combines peak detection, deconvolution, alignment, spectral annotation, normalization, statistics, and visualization, with particular support for data-independent MS/MS processing and lipid annotation.

tools.name: MSMS-Chooser
tools.summary: A GNPS workflow for automatically selecting candidate reference MS/MS spectra from LC-MS data of known standards using supplied molecular structures and expected precursor masses.
common_uses: Select MS/MS spectra corresponding to known standards from open-format data.
Prepare candidate reference spectra for validation and library contribution.

designed_for: Extracting candidate reference MS/MS scans when structures or formulas of standards are known.
requirements: Open-format mzML or mzXML data plus the MSMS-Chooser submission template.
considerations: Automated selections should be visually reviewed and validated before use as reference spectra.

tools.name: MZmine
tools.summary: An open-source desktop and command-line environment for processing, visualizing, and annotating mass spectrometry-based metabolomics data.
tools.description: MZmine is a modular environment for mass-spectrometry data processing with graphical and batch interfaces. It supports workflows spanning raw-data import, chromatogram construction, feature detection and resolving, alignment, ion and isotope grouping, quality filtering, visualization, spectral-library matching, and export to downstream annotation or networking resources.
common_uses: Detect, align, and filter features in untargeted LC-MS datasets.
Inspect chromatograms, spectra, ion-mobility data, and imaging-MS features.
Export feature and spectral data to annotation and molecular-networking resources.

designed_for: Modular processing and inspection of untargeted LC-MS datasets, including feature-based workflows that retain links to MS/MS and ion-mobility information.
Interactive and batch processing where users want a graphical environment with export to downstream annotation and molecular-networking tools.
not_designed_for: A replacement for every downstream structure-elucidation or statistical-analysis platform; specialist tools are commonly used after preprocessing.
requirements: Desktop installation; current releases bundle the runtime required to execute MZmine.
considerations: Parameter choices for feature detection, resolving, alignment, and filtering remain experiment dependent and should be documented in reproducible batch files.

tools.name: OpenMS
tools.summary: An open-source C++ library, command-line toolkit, and Python interface for reproducible mass spectrometry data processing in metabolomics and proteomics.
common_uses: Assemble reproducible command-line or Python workflows for LC-MS data processing.
Convert, inspect, detect, align, quantify, and annotate mass spectrometry features.

tools.name: ReDU
tools.summary: A repository-scale interface for finding, filtering, contextualizing, and reusing public tandem mass-spectrometry data through standardized sample metadata.
tools.description: ReDU links standardized sample information with public tandem mass-spectrometry datasets, enabling researchers to locate public files by organism, biospecimen, phenotype, disease state, and other metadata and to select data for reanalysis or co-analysis through GNPS.
common_uses: Filter public mass-spectrometry data by sample metadata.
Select public datasets for GNPS reanalysis or co-analysis.

designed_for: Contextualizing and reusing public tandem mass-spectrometry data using standardized metadata.
requirements: Repository records need sufficiently structured sample information to support the desired query.
considerations: Metadata completeness varies among historical public datasets.

tools.name: SIRIUS
tools.summary: A desktop and command-line framework for molecular-formula annotation, structure-database searching, compound-class prediction, and confidence estimation from tandem mass spectra.

access.notes: Local features and webservice-backed features have different access and licensing conditions. The official documentation should be checked for the current academic and commercial terms.

common_uses: Rank candidate molecular formulas from isotope and fragmentation patterns.
Search molecular-structure databases using predicted fingerprints.
Predict compound classes for spectra without confident structure matches.

designed_for: Molecular-formula and structure-candidate annotation from accurate-mass MS/MS data, including compound-class prediction when exact structures remain uncertain.
not_designed_for: Primary chromatographic feature detection and alignment; SIRIUS usually receives spectra or feature-associated MS/MS from upstream processing tools.
requirements: Some functions rely on SIRIUS web services and current access terms; users should consult the official documentation for academic and commercial conditions.
considerations: Candidate rankings are annotations rather than automatic confirmations of chemical identity; confidence and supporting evidence should be reported.

tools.description: SIRIUS is a desktop and command-line framework for annotating small molecules from high-resolution MS and MS/MS data. It combines isotope-pattern and fragmentation-tree analysis with molecular-formula ranking, CSI:FingerID structure-database searching, compound-class prediction, and confidence estimation.

tools.name: xcms
tools.summary: An open-source Bioconductor package for chromatographic mass spectrometry data preprocessing, feature detection, alignment, grouping, and visualization.
common_uses: Build scriptable preprocessing workflows for untargeted chromatographic MS data.
Detect chromatographic peaks and align retention times across samples.

designed_for: Reproducible, script-based preprocessing of LC-MS and GC-MS datasets in the R/Bioconductor ecosystem.
requirements: R and Bioconductor plus the package dependencies appropriate to the selected xcms release.
considerations: The package is code oriented rather than a standalone point-and-click workflow, so users benefit from basic R familiarity.

tools.description: xcms is a scriptable Bioconductor framework for processing chromatographically separated mass-spectrometry data in R. It provides algorithms for chromatographic peak detection, retention-time correction, correspondence/grouping across samples, filling missing feature intensities, and inspection of LC-MS and GC-MS datasets within reproducible analysis scripts.

protocols.name: Native MS metabolomics for metal-binding compounds
protocols.summary: A transferable LC-MS strategy that combines post-column pH adjustment and metal infusion with ion identity molecular networking to discover small molecules that bind metals in complex biological samples.
protocols.description: This protocol adapts native electrospray concepts to metabolomics so that protonated and metal-bound forms of the same chromatographic analyte can be detected together. Post-column pH adjustment and infusion of a selected metal are coupled to feature processing and ion identity molecular networking, allowing candidate metal-binding molecules to be prioritized from characteristic mass offsets and shared chromatographic behavior.

publication.title: Native mass spectrometry-based metabolomics identifies metal-binding compounds
publication.citation: Aron AT, Petras D, Schmid R, et al. Native mass spectrometry-based metabolomics identifies metal-binding compounds. Nature Chemistry 14, 100–109 (2022).

workflow_steps.title: Separate metabolites by LC
workflow_steps.description: Analyze the extract using an LC-MS method suitable for retaining native-like metal-binding interactions after chromatographic separation.

workflow_steps.title: Adjust post-column pH
workflow_steps.description: Infuse a volatile base or buffer after the LC column to establish conditions compatible with observing metal complexes during electrospray.

workflow_steps.title: Infuse the metal of interest
workflow_steps.description: Introduce a metal salt post-column so protonated and metal-bound forms of candidate ligands can be observed with matched retention behavior.

workflow_steps.title: Process features and ion identities
workflow_steps.description: Detect and align chromatographic features and group coeluting ion species with correlated peak shapes and expected mass relationships.

workflow_steps.title: Build an ion identity molecular network
workflow_steps.description: Use ion identity molecular networking to connect ion species and spectral relationships, highlighting candidate metal-binding compounds.

workflow_steps.title: Prioritize and validate candidate binders
workflow_steps.description: Interpret expected metal-adduct mass offsets, inspect spectra and chromatograms, and validate prioritized compounds with standards or orthogonal evidence where available.

tools.role: Feature detection, ion grouping, and ion identity networking preparation.
Ion identity molecular networking and MS/MS-based network analysis.
Public deposition and reuse of the study mass-spectrometry datasets.

designed_for: Discovering metal-binding small molecules in complex extracts using standard LC-MS hardware with post-column modification.
Comparing protonated and metal-bound ion species through chromatographic correlation and defined mass offsets.
requirements: LC-MS system with a post-column setup that permits pH adjustment and metal-salt infusion.
Appropriate blanks and controls to distinguish biologically relevant complexes from background or source-derived adducts.
considerations: Metal identity, pH, salt concentration and electrospray conditions can alter complex formation and should be optimized and reported.
The network highlights candidate binding behavior; structural identity and biological relevance require additional evidence.

protocols.name: Reverse metabolomics
protocols.summary: A discovery strategy that starts from a candidate chemical structure or reference MS/MS spectrum, searches public metabolomics repositories for matching spectra, and uses sample metadata to reveal biological or phenotypic associations.
protocols.description: Reverse metabolomics reverses the usual untargeted workflow. Instead of starting with an unknown feature and attempting to infer its structure, the researcher begins with a candidate structure and an experimental MS/MS spectrum, searches public metabolomics data for matching spectra, and then uses repository metadata to ask where the molecule occurs. The resulting organism, biospecimen, phenotype or disease associations can guide biological validation.

publication.title: Reverse metabolomics for the discovery of chemical structures from humans
publication.citation: Gentry EC, Collins SL, Panitchpakdi M, et al. Reverse metabolomics for the discovery of chemical structures from humans. Nature 626, 419–426 (2024).

workflow_steps.title: Generate or obtain a reference MS/MS spectrum
workflow_steps.description: Acquire tandem mass spectra for a candidate chemical structure, for example from a synthesized standard, authenticated standard, or suitable reference source.

workflow_steps.title: Select a representative reference spectrum
workflow_steps.description: When standards are analyzed in mixtures, automatically select the MS/MS scan associated with the expected precursor and review the spectrum before repository searching.

workflow_steps.title: Search public MS/MS data
workflow_steps.description: Use the reference spectrum as a query against public metabolomics datasets to identify files and datasets containing related spectra.

workflow_steps.title: Contextualize matches with sample metadata
workflow_steps.description: Summarize organism, biospecimen, phenotype, disease state and other standardized metadata associated with matching public files.

workflow_steps.title: Prioritize biological associations
workflow_steps.description: Use the distribution of matched spectra across public datasets to generate hypotheses about where the molecule occurs and which phenotypes or sample types it may be associated with.

workflow_steps.title: Validate prioritized associations
workflow_steps.description: Test the proposed association in independent cohorts, targeted measurements, culture systems, or functional experiments appropriate to the biological question.

tools.role: Selection of candidate reference MS/MS spectra from data acquired on standards.
Metadata-based contextualization of public mass-spectrometry matches.
Web infrastructure for spectral workflows and public-data analysis.
Public repository containing searchable metabolomics datasets.

designed_for: Asking where a known or newly synthesized chemical structure occurs across existing untargeted MS/MS datasets.
Using repository-scale metadata to generate hypotheses linking a molecule to organisms, sample types, disease states or other phenotypes.
requirements: A suitable reference MS/MS spectrum for the candidate molecule.
Public datasets with matching MS/MS signals and sufficient metadata to interpret biological context.
considerations: A repository spectral match is evidence of spectral similarity and occurrence, not by itself a complete structural confirmation.
Repository composition and metadata coverage can bias which biological contexts are visible.
